_note: The teleconsultation call: who is in the room, what each of them consented to, what a bad line does to a clinical decision, and what an encounter that did not finish is allowed to be called afterwards. Read by the web app; generated into Swift and Kotlin by scripts/emit-teleconsult.mjs. Nobody is named here — the doctor, the nurse and the patient are resolved from packages/catalog/vetting.json and the fixtures, so a registration number exists in one place. No clinician's refusal sentence is written here either: a doctor who may not consult is refused by can(subject, 'sign-clinical-review'), in the clinical queue's own words. Nothing in this file opens a camera, a microphone or a connection.

media.sentence: This build has never asked this device for the camera or the microphone. Neither permission is declared, no media of any kind is captured, and no connection is opened. What follows is the design of a consultation, drawn at full size.

states.name: Never asked
states.detail: MyThuso has not requested the camera or the microphone on this device. There is nothing to allow and nothing to withdraw, because no question was put to you.

states.name: You said no
states.detail: You were asked and you declined. The consultation is offered by voice on your phone line instead, and the refusal is remembered so you are not asked again every time.

states.name: Allowed
states.detail: You allowed it for consultations. It is used only while a call is running, and you can take it back in your phone's settings without telling us first.

media.whyTheDistinctionMatters: An app that shows the same screen for “we never asked” and “you refused” is telling you that your answer did not matter. They are different facts and they get different words.

identity.patientSideDetail: The person on the screen should be the doctor the booking named. Before the call opens, MyThuso shows you their name and their HPCSA registration number, read from the vetting record that was checked this morning — not typed into the booking by whoever made it. If the name on screen is not the name here, the call does not start.
identity.doctorSideDetail: The doctor asks for the six-digit visit code in the patient's own app — the same code a nurse is asked for at the door, for the same reason: a code the patient holds is a check the clinician cannot do without them. It changes for every visit and expires when the visit ends.
identity.failure: That code doesn’t match this visit. Call the Control Tower before continuing.
identity.whyOneMechanism: There is one identity check in MyThuso and this is it. A second mechanism invented for video would be a second thing to get wrong, and the one a patient had already learned would stop being the one that counts.

participants.name: The patient
participants.sees: The doctor, and anybody else on this list
participants.hears: Everyone on the call and everyone in the room
participants.note: The consultation is theirs. Everything below is a question put to them, not a setting configured for them.

participants.name: The doctor
participants.sees: Whatever the patient's camera is pointed at, and nothing else in the house
participants.consentQuestion: May this doctor see you and treat you on this call today?
participants.ifDeclined: There is no consultation. The call does not open, the booking is closed as declined, and the only thing written into your record is that you were asked and said no.
participants.note: The one person who cannot be asked to step out, because asking them to leave is the same as ending the call — and that is offered as its own button rather than dressed up as a roster change.

participants.name: The nurse
participants.where: In the room with the patient
participants.sees: The patient, the room, and the doctor on the screen
participants.hears: Everything said in the room and on the call
participants.consentQuestion: The nurse is in the room with you and will hear everything that is said. May she stay?
participants.ifDeclined: The nurse steps outside and waits. The consultation goes ahead without her, and the doctor is told plainly that there will be no examination and no readings taken during the call — because the only pair of hands in the room has just left it.
participants.note: This is the case a private doctor's appointment does not have, and the one most video-consultation products have no words for at all.

participants.name: A parent or guardian
participants.where: In the room with the patient
participants.sees: The patient, the room, and the doctor on the screen
participants.hears: Everything said in the room and on the call
participants.consentQuestion: Your guardian is in the room and will hear everything. May they stay?
participants.ifDeclined: Where the patient may consent to their own treatment, the guardian leaves the room and the consultation continues. Where they may not, the consultation is stopped and rebooked rather than held in private with a child who cannot consent to it.
participants.note: A guardian's authority to be present is verified in the vetting register, and it is still a question put to the patient rather than an answer given on their behalf.

participants.name: An interpreter
participants.where: On the call, from somewhere else
participants.hears: Everything said in the room and on the call
participants.consentQuestion: An interpreter is on this call and will hear everything you tell the doctor. May they stay?
participants.ifDeclined: The interpreter leaves the call. If you and the doctor do not share a language, the consultation is rebooked with a different interpreter — it is not continued in a language you did not choose, because a consultation you cannot follow is not consultation.
participants.note: An interpreter hears the whole consultation, including the parts a patient would not have said in front of a neighbour. They are named, they are bound by the same confidentiality as the clinicians, and they are consented to like anybody else.

consent.revokedMidCall: The call ends at the moment it is said. It is not held open to finish the notes, and the notes are finished — if at all — from what was already said.
The nurse steps out, and the doctor is told the room no longer has a clinician in it. Anything that needed hands is rebooked.
The guardian leaves the room. Where the patient cannot consent for themselves, the call is stopped instead.
The interpreter leaves the call. If the doctor and the patient cannot understand one another, the consultation is stopped and rebooked.

Recording stops at the moment it is said, and what was captured before that moment is destroyed rather than kept for the part that was consented to. A recording that outlives its consent is a recording nobody gave.

recording.decision: This preview does not offer recording, and it does not offer a switch for it either.
recording.why: Consent to a consultation is not consent to a recording, and the honest way to hold that apart is to ask twice. But this build has no microphone permission, no camera permission and nowhere to put a recording, so a recording switch here would be a control that cannot do what it says — and a patient who is taught to tick it in a preview has been taught to tick it. A refusal is easier to design honestly than a promise: what the screen does instead is say what a recording would be for, who could open it, how long it would live and how it would be asked for, so that the design can be argued with before anything can be captured.
instead: The written consultation record is the record. It is the same structure a nurse's visit and a doctor's review write into, and it is what a later clinician actually reads.

Who was in the room, and what each of them was consented to, is written into the record with the consultation — because “was anyone else listening” is a question a patient may ask a year later and deserve an answer to.
A patient who wants a copy of what was decided is given the written record, which is legible, correctable and does not carry the sound of their own voice.

whenItExists.askedSeparately: It is a second question, on its own screen, after consent to the consultation and before the call opens. It is never a checkbox underneath the first one, because a checkbox underneath the first one is answered by the momentum of the first one.
whenItExists.refusingIsCostless: Saying no changes nothing at all about the care you receive. The consultation goes ahead, with the same doctor, at the same time, for the same money, and nobody is told you refused.
whenItExists.whileRecording: A red bar across the top of the screen for the whole time it runs, on every participant's device, saying who started it and that it can be stopped. It cannot be minimised, dismissed or hidden behind anything.
whoMayView: You, from your own account, whenever you want
The doctor who held the consultation, under their own registration
Nobody else without a written request that appears in your access history before it is granted
whenItExists.afterwards: Destroyed after 30 days, automatically, whether or not anybody has watched it. The written record is what is kept under the clinical retention schedule — a recording is evidence of a conversation, not the record of a decision, and keeping it for years would make every consultation a permanent tape of somebody's worst afternoon.

clinicalLimits.name: Take a history
clinicalLimits.detail: What the patient reports, in their own words. This is most of a consultation and it survives a bad line.

clinicalLimits.name: See how the patient looks
clinicalLimits.detail: Breathing, colour, distress, whether they can finish a sentence. A doctor who cannot see this says so rather than assuming it is fine.

clinicalLimits.name: Assess something visible
clinicalLimits.detail: A rash, a wound, swelling, a drooping face. On a poor picture this is refused rather than guessed at, because a wound seen through four frames a second is a wound not seen.

clinicalLimits.name: Read a label or a document
clinicalLimits.detail: A pill box, a clinic card, a discharge letter held up to the camera.

clinicalLimits.name: Ask the nurse to examine
clinicalLimits.detail: The doctor asks; the nurse examines and reports. The finding is the nurse's, recorded under her name, and the doctor never writes it up as their own examination.

clinicalLimits.name: Reach and sign a decision
clinicalLimits.detail: A decision needs enough of the above to stand behind, and the doctor says in the record which of it they had. A decision reached on sound alone is written as a decision reached on sound alone.

connection.name: Video and sound
connection.patientSees: The doctor, and yourself in the corner. Everything is working.
connection.doctorSees: The patient, and the room behind them.
connection.note: The state everything else is measured against, and the rarest of the four on a South African mobile network at five in the afternoon.

connection.name: The connection is poor
connection.patientSees: The picture is breaking up. You can still be heard. The doctor knows.
connection.doctorSees: The picture is breaking up at the patient's end. Do not rely on what you can see.
connection.note: A first-class state with its own screen, not a toast. Both ends are told the same thing at the same time, and the doctor is offered the drop to sound only rather than left to fight the picture. Something looked at through a breaking picture is not something examined, so assessing a wound and reading a label are withdrawn here — the doctor asks the nurse, or asks the patient to be seen.

connection.name: Sound only
connection.patientSees: Sound only. This uses far less of your data and works on a weak signal. It is a normal way to hold a consultation.
connection.doctorSees: Sound only. You are not seeing this patient. Anything you record about how they look is the nurse's finding or the patient's own words.
connection.note: Designed for, not fallen back to. Bandwidth in South Africa is a constraint on most of the country most of the time, and a product that treats sound as a failure state is a product that works in Sandton.

connection.name: The call dropped
connection.patientSees: The call has dropped. Stay where you are — the doctor is calling you back. You do not have to do anything.
connection.doctorSees: The line dropped at the patient's end. Do not close this encounter. Call back, then call the number on the booking.
connection.note: A clinical event, not a network event. The encounter stays open, nothing about it is concluded, and the screen at both ends says the same thing about whose job it is to fix it.

reconnect.whoCallsWhom: The doctor calls back. The patient does nothing, and is told they do not have to — a person who has just lost signal is the person least able to re-establish it, and asking them to redial makes the failure their fault.
reconnect.duringTheHold: The encounter stays open on the doctor's screen for the whole hold, and cannot be closed as finished while it is running. The patient's screen counts the same seconds down, so neither of them is waiting on nothing.
reconnect.afterTheHold: A phone call to the number on the booking, on the ordinary telephone network, which works where data does not.
reconnect.ifUnreachable: The encounter is closed as interrupted and not resumed, the patient is offered the next available slot without losing their place, and nothing is charged. A note goes to the Control Tower, because three of these from one address in a week is a coverage problem rather than three unlucky patients.
reconnect.nurseInTheRoom: If a nurse is in the room she stays with the patient for the whole hold, tells them what is happening, and does not leave the house on the assumption that the call will come back. If the patient was unwell enough for the doctor to be worried before the line dropped, she escalates on the nurse's own pathway rather than waiting.
reconnect.whyNotLonger: Ninety seconds is long enough for a network to recover and short enough that nobody sits looking at a spinner wondering whether they have been forgotten. After it, a person tells them what is happening.

outcomes.name: Consultation completed
outcomes.record: A signed consultation in the standard structure, attributed to the doctor's HPCSA registration, carrying who was present and what each of them was consented to.

outcomes.name: Interrupted, then finished
outcomes.record: A signed consultation, and the interruption on the face of it: when the line dropped, how long it was down, and that the doctor confirmed the visit code again before continuing. A break in a consultation is a clinical fact and it is not tidied away.

outcomes.name: Interrupted and not resumed
outcomes.record: An interrupted encounter. It carries who was present, what was said before the line dropped, and the fact that no assessment and no plan were reached. There is no assessment field, no plan field and no signature block, because nobody may sign a decision they did not get to make — and an encounter with a signature on it reads, a year later, exactly like one that finished.

outcomes.name: Never connected
outcomes.record: That the appointment was attempted and no connection was ever made. Nothing clinical, because nothing clinical happened.

outcomes.name: Consent declined
outcomes.record: That consent was asked for and not given. A declined consultation is a valid outcome, not a failed one, and the reason is not recorded unless the patient offers it.

outcomes.name: Identity not confirmed
outcomes.record: That the visit code did not match and the consultation did not open. The same refusal as the nurse at the door: it stops, it does not warn and continue.

outcomes.name: The clinician may not consult
outcomes.record: That the call was not opened because the doctor's standing did not allow it, and the patient was rebooked with a doctor whose registration is current. The patient is told the appointment is moving, and is not told which check failed — a lapsed registration is the doctor's business with their council.

rules.title: Everyone who can hear you is on the list
rules.sentence: Everyone who can see or hear you is named on this screen, with their role and where they are, before the call opens. Nobody joins a MyThuso consultation without appearing here, and you can ask anyone except the doctor to leave at any moment, without giving a reason.

rules.title: Being seen is not being recorded
rules.sentence: Agreeing to a consultation is not agreeing to a recording. They are two questions asked at two different moments, and saying no to the second costs you nothing: the same doctor, the same appointment, the same price, and nobody is told you refused.

rules.title: A dropped call is not a finished one
rules.sentence: A call that dropped is not a consultation that ended. Until a doctor has reached a decision and signed it, this is an interrupted encounter in your record — it says so in those words, it carries no diagnosis, and it is never charged for.

rules.title: Sound only is a consultation
rules.sentence: Sound only is an ordinary way to be seen in South Africa, not a failure. What changes is not how seriously you are taken but what the doctor is allowed to conclude on their own, and this screen says which of those things they still can.

rules.title: A doctor on a screen examines nothing
rules.sentence: On a call the doctor examines nobody. Anything felt, measured or looked at closely is the nurse's finding, recorded under her name and her SANC registration — never written up afterwards as the doctor's own examination.

rules.title: Nothing here is connected
rules.sentence: MyThuso has never asked this device for the camera or the microphone, and this build declares neither permission. That is not the same as you refusing: no question was put to you, so there is nothing to withdraw.

refusals.sentence: Nobody sits in on a MyThuso consultation to learn. A student, a supervisor or a quality reviewer is a person in the room, and a person in the room is named, asked for and consented to — or they are not there.

There is no way to record a consultation without the recording being visible on every participant's screen for the whole time it runs. An indicator that can be dismissed is a recording nobody consented to.

A consultation is not held open “just to finish the notes” after consent is withdrawn. Withdrawal ends the call at the moment it is said, and what is written afterwards is written only from what was already said.

A doctor does not record a finding about something they could not see or hear. On a poor line an uncertain answer is written down as an uncertain answer and the patient is seen again — a confident note is not a substitute for a working connection.

An encounter that never reached a decision is not charged for, whoever's connection failed. Making a patient pay for their own bad signal puts the cost of South African bandwidth on the person least able to do anything about it.

An interrupted encounter is never closed off as a completed consultation, and no clinician is offered a button that would do it. A record that cannot tell a finished consultation from an abandoned one is worse than no record, because it will be trusted.
